title: Damage Debuff
wikitext_excerpt:
{{BuffInfobox
|name = Damage Debuff
|image = Transparent.png
|type = Debuff
|display = N/A
}}

==Description==
The '''Damage Debuff''' is a debuff applied by enemies that decreases a tower's damage. This debuff does not appear anywhere on the tower, though it does reduce the percentage of the tower's [[Damage Buff]].

==Mechanics==
The '''Damage Debuff''' effectively is just a negative [[Damage Buff]], best seen if a tower affected by it has a [[Damage Buff]]. For example, if a tower with a 20% [[Damage Buff]] receives a 15% '''Damage Debuff''', the [[Damage Buff]] will get reduced to 5%. Similarly, if a tower receives a '''Damage Debuff''' higher than its current [[Damage Buff]], the icon for it will be removed entirely. For example, if a tower with a 50% [[Damage Buff]] will receive a 60% '''Damage Debuff''', the icon for the buff will disappear and the tower will end up with a 10% '''Damage Debuff'''.

The damage affected by the '''Damage Debuff''' is calculated as:
::<big>'''Damage × (1 - (Damage Debuff - [[Damage Buff]]))'''</big>
:::where '''Damage Debuff''' and [[Damage Buff]] is the debuff supplied by the enemy in decimal form (for example, 10% is 0.1). If the tower has no [[Damage Buff]] on itself, the number for it should be set to 0.

The damage of a tower affected by the '''Damage Debuff''' cannot be in decimal form, instead of being rounded down or rounded up to the nearest integer. For example, a tower that deals 5 damage with a 50% '''Damage Debuff''' will deal 2 damage, instead of 2.5. The damage also cannot be lower than 1. For example, a tower with a 25% debuff will have its damage displayed as 0.75, but it will actually deal 1 damage, though some towers like the [[Shotgunner]] will break and actually deal nan damage.

==Applied By==
The following event enemies can apply the '''Damage Debuff''' to towers:
*[[Null Missile APC]] (''Null Missile Barrage'' ability, [[Null & Void Event|Null & Void]])
*[[Null Pursuit]] (''Missile Attack'' ability, [[Null & Void Event|Null & Void]])
*[[Rift Walker]] (''Dimensional Discharge'' ability, [[Null & Void Event|Null & Void]])
*[[Missile Ducky]] (''Widespread Terrorism'' ability, [[Ducky Revenge Event|Ducky Revenge]])

==Update History==
*'''31 October 2025''' - [[v1.79.0]]
**'''Damage Debuff''' added.

It also plays a powering down sound when it dies. ==Strategy== *When dealing with the '''Shotgunner''' when it first debuts, high DPS towers are best. ==Description==
The '''Damage Buff''' is a buff that increases a tower's damage, making them stronger. It is displayed on the tower itself with the icon of an arm with muscle.

==Mechanics==
'''Damage Buff''' range reduction is calculated as:
::<big>'''Damage × (1 + Damage Buff)'''</big>
:::where '''Damage Buff''' is the debuff supplied in decimal form (for example, 10% is 0.1).

The damage increased by the '''Damage Buff''' will always round down to the nearest integer. For example, a tower that deals 5 damage with a 50% '''Damage Buff''' will deal 7 damage, instead of 7.5.

Multiple towers are not fully affected by the buff. A full list of towers affected fully, partially or that are unaffected can be found below.
{{DamageBuff}}

==Description==
The '''Range Buff''' is a buff that increases a tower's range. It is shown on the tower with a blue icon of multiple waves.

==Mechanics==
'''Range Buff''' range reduction is calculated as:
::<big>'''Range × (1 + Range Buff)'''</big>
:::where '''Range Buff''' is the buff supplied in decimal form (for example, 10% is 0.1).

The range of a tower affected by the '''Range Buff''' can be in decimal form, instead of being rounded down or rounded up to the nearest interger. For example, a tower with 5 range with a 50% '''Range Buff''' will have a range of 7.5.

The following towers are either partially or fully not affected by the '''Range Buff''':
*All [[units]].
*The [[Shotgunner]], as its bullets do not extend into the increased range.
*The [[DJ Booth]] cannot have its range boosted by another [[DJ Booth]].
**Other range buff sources, like the [[Ranger]], can still apply it.
*Circling range of the [[Pursuit]] and [[Ace Pilot]].
**The radius in which towers gain hidden detection from the [[Ace Pilot]] also cannot be increased.
**These towers' attack range can still be increased.
*The sentry building range of the [[Engineer]].
*The deadzone ranges of towers like the [[Biologist]] and [[Engineer]].
**The attack range for these towers can still be increased.
*Secondary orange range of towers like the range buff range for the [[Ranger]] or the gravestone range for the [[Necromancer]].
**The main range of these towers can still be increased.
*The chain range of the [[Electroshocker]].
**The attack range can still be increased.
*The explosion radius from [[Splash Damage|Splash Damage towers]] cannot be increased.

==Applied By==
The following towers or consumables can apply the '''Range Buff''' to other towers:
*[[DJ Booth]] (Passive)
*[[Ranger]] (Passive for 20 seconds at the beginning of each wave)
*[[Range Flag]] (Passive)
*[[UAV]] (Passive)
*[[Easter Egg]] (Passive for 20 seconds)
The following event features can apply the '''Range Buff''' to towers:

* [[The Moon]] (Passive, [[Null & Void Event|Null & Void]])

The following towers used to have the '''Range Buff''':
*{{Color|Golden}} [[Pyromancer]] (Passive)
*{{Color|Golden}} [[Cowboy]] (Passive)
*[[Slasher]] (Old ''Knife Throw'' ability)

The following removed towers had the '''Range Buff''':

title: Firerate Bug
wikitext_excerpt:
{{Removed|date = 6th of June 2026}}
{{Improve|this page and majority of tower/unit pages require updating}}
The '''Firerate Bug''', also known as the '''RoF (Rate of Fire) Bug''', was a bug that slightly increased the firerate of all towers and units. This increase was not displayed on the statistics in the game. This bug significantly affected the statistics of fast-firing towers, such as the [[Minigunner]] and [[Ace Pilot]], by significantly decreasing their DPS, whereas slow-firing towers like the [[Ranger]] or [[Sniper]] were hardly affected.

This has been fixed as of the 6th of June 2026, and all firerate statistics in the game are considered to be accurate unless affected by a different unrelated bug.

{{RightTOC}}

==Prior to 5th of June 2026==
The '''Firerate Bug''' affects all towers and units that can directly attack enemies, meaning the only towers that are not affected are the [[Farm]], [[Medic]] and the [[Firework Technician]] and the only units that are not affected are the [[Humvee]], [[Humvee 2]], [[Elf]], [[Bomber Elf (Unit)|Bomber Elf]], [[Skeleton (Unit)|Skeleton]], [[Giant Skeleton (Unit)|Giant Skeleton]] and [[Hallow Guard (Unit)|Hallow Guard]]. The '''Firerate Bug''' does not affect the firerate of some secondary attacks towers or units may perform, some damage-over-time effects applied by towers (like burn from the [[Pyromancer]]) or certain other cooldowns.

The '''Firerate Bug''' increases the firerate of a tower/unit depending on its firerate, which can vary anywhere between 0.017 and 0.032 seconds. The firerate increase affects fast firing towers the most; for example, the [[Minigunner]] at Level 4 should have a firerate of 0.09, but because of the '''Firerate Bug''', it has a firerate of about 0.117, decreasing its DPS from 166.67 to 128.20, which is a decrease of 38.47 DPS, or a loss of about 23.08 DPS. Meanwhile, slow firing towers are barely affected by it; for example, the [[Ranger]] at Level 4 should have a firerate of 8, but because of the '''Firerate Bug''', it has a firerate of about 8.025, decreasing its DPS from 156.26 to 155.76, which is a decrease of 0.30 DPS, or a loss of 0.2% DPS.

The [[Firerate Buff]] is also affected by the '''Firerate Bug''', making it less effective. For example, the Level 4 [[Minigunner]] without the '''Firerate Bug''' with a 50% firerate boost should have a firerate of 0.06, but with the '''Firerate Bug''' it has a firerate of 0.083. This means that its DPS with a 50% firerate boost is decreased from 250 to 180.72, which is a decrease of 69.28 DPS, or a loss of 27.71% DPS.

On this Wiki, the firerate statistic of all towers and units is increased by specific values based on the firerate. While technically possible to calculate by hand, due to the effort it would take, it is overall recommended to either use [[Help:Neowtext#ROFBUG|Neowtext]] or [https://fiheron.github.io/dps-calc/ an online calculator].

==Prior to the 9th of January 2023==
Prior to the 9th of January 2023, the firerate increase caused by the '''Firerate Bug''' for units was higher than it currently is. The firerate increase was generally around 0.03 seconds. For towers, the firerate increase remained at around 0.008 seconds.

On this Wiki, the firerate statistic of all towers and units after the [[V1.6.0|Violent Night Update]] and before the 9th of January 2023 is increased by 0.008 and 0.03 respectively, unless stated otherwise. This does not, however, mean the actual value is this; it can vary between towers and even between matches.

==Prior to the Violent Night Update==
Prior to the [[V1.6.0|Violent Night Update]], the firerate increase caused by the '''Firerate Bug''' for units was lower than it was before the [[V1.6.0|Violent Night Update]]. The firerate increases could be anywhere between 0.008 and 0.017 seconds, but the increase was generally around 0.008 seconds. This is the same as the current situation.

{{Knockback}}Knockback |sandbox = Yes |tag = {{AttrTag|Second|Fly.png|Flying}} }} ==Description== '''Flying''' is an enemy type that makes the enemy fly above the path, making them avoid being damaged by most things on the path. Towers need flying detection to target these enemies. ==Mechanics== '''Flying''' enemies fly above the path, which grants them multiple perks. The main immunity that it grants is requiring flying detection to target them, making it difficult for towers without said detection to damage a '''Flying''' enemy. '''Flying''' enemies have various other unique immunities that are applied, outside of flying detection: # They are completely immune to being damaged by unit collision damage, even if they would normally collide with each other. #*This includes the [[Gift Bomber]], which cannot collide with '''Flying''' enemies, despite visually passing through '''Flying''' enemies. #*Some units, like the [[Rifleman]] or [[Missile APC]], can detect flying enemies, even if they cannot collide with them. #They are able to fly over road hazards, namely the [[Trapper]]'s traps and the [[Harvester]]'s thorns (and by extension the [[Farm]]'s). #*The [[Commando]]'s missiles, can still affect them. #*The [[Barricade]] can collide with '''Flying''' enemies, but they deal unit collision damage. Therefore, '''Flying''' enemies are also immune to this. #They are immune to being knocked back by towers. This does not mean they are immune to other effects from attacks that knock back enemies. #*For example, the [[DJ Booth]] can still slow down '''Flying''' enemies, even if the purple track cannot knock them back. '''Flying''' enemies may be indirectly damaged by towers, even if they do not have flying detection. For example, the [[Brawler]]'s ''Reposition'' ability deals damage to '''Flying''' enemies, though due to their knockback immunity it does not knock them back. Build up chill to slow and freeze enemies in their tracks!|Store Description}} |-|Version 3 = {{QuoteBox|Chill enemies to a slow freeze!|Store Description}} |-|Version 2 = {{QuoteBox|Shoot an ice beam, freezing targets for a few seconds.|Store Description}} |-|Version 1 = {{QuoteBox|Freeze zombies temporarily with a freeze ray!|Former Store Description}} }} __TOC__ ==Description== The '''Freezer''' is a ground [[Towers|tower]] that fires an ice beam and applies chill and slow down enemies, freezing at later levels. It can be bought in the store for {{Coins|650}}. The '''Freezer''' targets a single enemy and fires a ''Frost Ray'', chilling the enemy and slowing it down. The chillness slowness effect stacks with each hit multiple times. This chillness effect also deals damage over time, chipping away the health of enemies affected by it. Starting from Level 2, it can freeze enemies. When the chillness slowness effect is higher than the max slowdown, the enemy will be frozen, which generally when targeting a single enemy takes four or five shots. Larger enemies will be frozen for a shorter amount of time than average sized enemies. Enemies with [[Freeze Immunity]] also cannot be frozen, slowed down or have their defense dropped by the '''Freezer'''. At Level 3+, the '''Freezer''' fires in bursts, with a short delay between them. Additionally, at Level 3+, it drops defense by 10% every tick. It can only decrease an enemy's defense by 33%. For example, if an enemy has 50% defense, it will be decreased by 16%. On top of this, it will also start dealing damage over time with its chill at Level 3. Additionally at Level 4, the '''Freezer''' gains the ability to throw a '''Frost Grenade''', freezing enemies within an explosion radius. The '''Freezer''' does well as an all-rounder support tower. Due to its generally low price and decent DPS, the '''Freezer''' can be a solid choice for early-game defense to mid game with very good cost efficiency. Towards late game, the '''Freezer''' is useful for stalling, defense melting and deal additional DPS through its damage over time, though its DPS is insufficient to deal with late-game waves alone. The '''Freezer''' has [[Lead (Attribute)|lead]] detection from Level 0 and [[Hidden (Attribute)|hidden]] detection from level 2.
